title: Core phrases
done when: Without looking, you can greet, thank, apologize, and ask someone to repeat or slow down, at the polite tier.

title: Language foundations
done when: You can build a new sentence from a pattern template by swapping the bracketed slot, and say which politeness tier you used.

title: Pronunciation
done when: You can read a phrase you have not seen aloud from its transliteration and name the sounds English speakers get wrong.

title: Writing system
done when: You can recognize the characters and marks the chapter covers on a sign or a menu and say what they change.

title: Directions and navigation
done when: You can ask where something is, follow the answer, and confirm you understood it, in writing, from memory.

title: Transportation
done when: You can buy a ticket, ask which platform or stop, and tell a driver where to go and where to stop.

title: Restaurants
done when: You can get a table, order with a substitution or an allergy, and ask for the bill, start to finish.

title: Shopping
done when: You can ask for a size or a color, ask the price, and decline politely.

title: Hotels
done when: You can check in, report a problem with the room, and check out.

title: Cultural guide
done when: For three situations in the chapter you can say what to do, what not to do, and the phrase that goes with it.
